intro: The closing conversation of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: opinions and wishes about work, study and living — what you think, why, and what you would do if. Copy the exercise in, say 'Los geht's', answer in full sentences; the score and corrections come at the end. The tutor listens for the building blocks of a real argument: an opinion with a reason (Ich finde …, weil …), a hypothetical with the Konjunktiv II on both sides (Wenn ich …, würde ich …), a contrast (obwohl / trotzdem), and adjectives with endings in your descriptions. This is a real discussion in miniature, so also practise the moves of a discussion: agree, disagree politely, ask your partner what they think.
tips[0].title: Opinion + reason + question back
tips[0].text: Ich bin der Meinung, dass …, weil … Und was denkst du? Three moves in one turn keep a discussion going and hit three marking criteria.
tips[0].check.why: It has all three moves: an opinion, a reason with weil, and a question back to your partner.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Opinion
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Reason
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Ask back
tips[1].title: Disagree with a cushion
tips[1].text: Das stimmt, aber … · Da bin ich nicht ganz deiner Meinung, weil … · Einerseits hast du recht, andererseits … Never a bare 'Nein'.
tips[1].check.why: Disagree with a cushion: accept part of the point first (Das stimmt, aber …), then give your view.
tips[2].title: One wenn-sentence per topic
tips[2].text: Wenn ich die Wahl hätte, würde ich … — drop one hypothetical into each topic and the Konjunktiv is covered.
tips[2].check.why: An unreal wenn-sentence uses the Konjunktiv on both sides: hätte in the wenn-clause, würde in the main clause.
exam: A discussion like this is part of the B1 speaking exam — and of every conversation where you want your view heard.
hook: Give your opinion, push back politely and imagine 'what if' with wenn … würde: the three moves of any good discussion.
